title: Football transfer rumours: Keylor Navas to Manchester City?
trail: Anthony Martial to Sevilla? | Kane and Salah reject Real Madrid? | Divock Origi to Borussia Dortmund?
body: Once upon a time Real Madrid could attract any player they wanted. Who Real want, Real get – that’s what the old folks used to say. But times have changed. Those three consecutive Champions League titles were but a death rattle. Today we are told by El Pais that interest from Real have recently and emphatically been rebuffed by both Mo Salah and Harry Kane. Those rejections, on the back of Zinedine Zidane walking away and Cristiano Ronaldo bidding adieu, are being interpreted by at least one rash gossip column as signs of a terminal decline. That’s what this wheeze of moving a La Liga fixture to America is all about: Real are stealthily packing in football and will relocate to the US to gradually morph into a baseball franchise. As a football club, they are done. Or maybe Kane just really loves Spurs, and Salah didn’t fancy seeing Sergio Ramos every morning. It’s hard to say for sure. The Mill isn’t pretending to have all the answers here. We can tell you this, though: Manchester City are thinking of rescuing Keylor Navas from the sinking ship that is Real Madrid. Following Claudio Bravo’s injury, City are exploring the possibility of getting the Costa Rican goalkeeper on an emergency loan so that City’s stars don’t have to worry their heads about what will happen if Ederson doesn’t recover from the shock of conceding at home to Huddersfield. Elsewhere, Manchester United are also in terminal decline, plainly. And it’s all the fault of that over-promoted suit Ed Woodward, according to some fans. The word is those fans are going to make their feelings known through the medium of a banner trailed for an airplane during Monday’s match against Spurs. The Mill has not heard anything to suggest José Mourinho has applied for a pilot’s licence but we’ll keep you posted. Anthony Martial could be allowed to hightail it out of Old Trafford by the end of the month if Sevilla come up with a good enough offer. The ambitious Spanish club are also trying to prise Julian Draxler from PSG, who, in turn, are considering bolstering their defence by freeing both Toby Alderweireld and Danny Rose from Spurs. Meanwhile, PSG are trying to persuade Adrien Rabiot to sign a new contract before his current deal expires next year but the midfielder is playing hard to get so that he will be easy to get for someone else next summer. Barcelona are said to be keen on him. The former Chelsea midfielder Ramires, scorer of a famous Champions League goal against Barcelona, reckons he has had all the fun he could possibly have playing for Jiangsu Suning so the 31-year-old wants to move back to a European club now before it’s too late. Marseille are preparing to grant his wish. Chelsea’s Brazilian winger Lucas Piazon may also be heading to France, as Reims have the hots for him. Borussia Dortmund may be willing to offer Divock Origi a fresh start following his fall to the bottom of Liverpool’s pecking order. Waistcoat supermodel Gareth Southgate is considering handing a full England cap to 18-year-old Phil Foden. Just don’t call the exciting young midfielder the new Jack Rodwell, whatever you do. Speaking of whom, Rodwell is is said to be close to agreeing a deal to join Blackburn Rovers. Another free agent, James Collins, who turns 35 today, is said to be close to returning to West Ham three months after being told via email that his time was up. Now that would be a revival to give hope even to Real Madrid.
